questions.question: Explain the difference between an interest rate and interest, using Zanele's savings account as the example, and state the unit each one carries.
questions.expected_answer: The interest rate is a percentage per time period — 6% per year — a speed, not money. The interest is the rand amount produced when the rate acts on the principal: 6% of R4 000 is R240. Rates carry percent per period; interest carries rand.

questions.question: Show, year by year, how R4 000 at 6% per year grows over two years when the interest stays in the account, and explain why year two's interest is larger.
questions.expected_answer: Year one: 6% of R4 000 is R240, balance R4 240. Year two: 6% of R4 240 is R254,40, balance R4 494,40. Year two is larger because the first year's interest remained in the account and itself earned interest — the balance, not the original deposit, is what the rate acts on.

questions.question: Why can the mashonisa's 25% not be compared directly with the bank's 15%, and what is the honest comparison?
questions.expected_answer: The periods differ: 15% is per year, 25% is per month. On R4 000 the bank charges R600 per year while the mashonisa charges R1 000 every month. Converted to the same period, 25% per month is 300% per year — twenty times the bank's 15%. Rates must wear the same time period before being compared.
